original_title: Layoff-blasted Fallout game studio announces it's building Fallout 5 from the rubble
summary_en: Despite recent workforce reductions, Bethesda Game Studios is moving forward with the highly anticipated Fallout 5. This announcement comes as the franchise experiences a resurgence in popularity thanks to its hit TV adaptation.
ai_analysis: Bethesda's bold move to announce Fallout 5 amidst layoffs highlights the franchise's immense value and the studio's commitment to its core IPs, even as it navigates challenging internal transitions.

en.title: Fallout 5 Officially Confirmed by Bethesda Amidst Layoffs
en.summary: Despite recent workforce reductions, Bethesda Game Studios is moving forward with the highly anticipated Fallout 5. This announcement comes as the franchise experiences a resurgence in popularity thanks to its hit TV adaptation.
en.body:
In a move that surprised many given recent industry turbulence, **Bethesda Game Studios** has officially announced that **Fallout 5** is entering pre-production. This marks the first main-series installment in the beloved post-apocalyptic RPG franchise since **Fallout 4** launched in 2015. The news comes as the studio, owned by Microsoft, was impacted by sweeping layoffs across its Xbox gaming division, though reports indicate Bethesda lost 'dozens' of staff rather than hundreds.

The timing of the announcement is certainly striking, with **Bethesda** studio head **Todd Howard** confirming the plans to Bloomberg News. It's a defiant declaration of intent, pushing forward with one of the most ambitious projects in the studio's history at a moment that could easily be perceived as precarious. This bold step is undoubtedly fueled by the massive resurgence in interest surrounding the **Fallout** universe, largely propelled by the critical and commercial success of Prime Video's television adaptation.

## Rebuilding from the Rubble

The confirmation of **Fallout 5** is a beacon of hope for fans who have been eagerly awaiting a new mainline entry. It also arrives alongside news that remasters of **Fallout 3** and **Fallout: New Vegas** are officially in development, further cementing **Bethesda**'s commitment to the franchise. While details on the development partners for these remasters are still emerging, the involvement of **Obsidian Entertainment** in a new **Fallout** project has also been hinted at, suggesting a collaborative effort to expand the wasteland.

This strategic pivot, especially with reports suggesting **Microsoft** is re-focusing **Obsidian**'s efforts towards **Fallout**, indicates a clear prioritization of the franchise's future. It’s a significant decision that could shape the direction of future **Fallout** games, potentially blending **Bethesda**'s established approach with **Obsidian**'s narrative strengths, as seen in the critically acclaimed **Fallout: New Vegas**.

## A Fallout Renaissance

For fans, the announcement is a double-edged sword. On one hand, the prospect of a new **Fallout** game is exhilarating, especially with the momentum generated by the TV show. On the other, the context of recent layoffs casts a shadow, raising questions about the development pipeline and the impact on **Bethesda**'s workforce. The union representing **Bethesda** employees highlighted that the layoffs affected programmers, artists, designers, and testers, underscoring the human cost behind these ambitious announcements. Nevertheless, the sheer enthusiasm for **Fallout 5** and the confirmed remasters suggests a strong community desire to return to the irradiated landscapes, regardless of the behind-the-scenes challenges.

## What's Next

While **Fallout 5** is confirmed to be in pre-production, specific release windows or platforms have not yet been announced. Fans can expect more details to emerge as **Bethesda Game Studios** continues to outline its long-term roadmap, which also includes **The Elder Scrolls VI** as a primary development focus.

es.title: Fallout 5: Bethesda confirma el juego más esperado
es.summary: A pesar de los recientes despidos, Bethesda Game Studios avanza con Fallout 5, el juego más esperado de la franquicia postapocalíptica. La noticia llega en un momento de resurgimiento de la serie gracias a su exitosa adaptación televisiva.
es.body:
La noticia ha sorprendido a muchos debido a la reciente turbulencia en la industria, **Bethesda Game Studios** ha anunciado oficialmente que **Fallout 5** ha entrado en preproducción. Esto marca el primer juego principal de la serie desde que **Fallout 4** se lanzó en 2015. La noticia llega mientras el estudio, propiedad de **Microsoft**, se vio afectado por despidos generalizados en su división de juegos **Xbox**, aunque los informes indican que **Bethesda** perdió 'decenas' de empleados en lugar de cientos.

## Reconstruyendo desde las ruinas

La confirmación de **Fallout 5** es un faro de esperanza para los fanáticos que han estado esperando ansiosamente una nueva entrega principal. También llega junto con la noticia de que las remasterizaciones de **Fallout 3** y **Fallout: New Vegas** están oficialmente en desarrollo, lo que refuerza aún más el compromiso de **Bethesda** con la franquicia. Aunque los detalles sobre los socios de desarrollo para estas remasterizaciones aún están surgiendo, la participación de **Obsidian Entertainment** en un nuevo proyecto **Fallout** también ha sido insinuado, lo que sugiere un esfuerzo colaborativo para expandir el paisaje postapocalíptico.

## Un renacimiento de Fallout

Para los fanáticos, el anuncio es una espada de doble filo. Por un lado, la perspectiva de un nuevo juego **Fallout** es emocionante, especialmente con el impulso generado por el show de televisión. Por otro lado, el contexto de los recientes despidos proyecta una sombra, planteando preguntas sobre la línea de desarrollo y el impacto en la fuerza laboral de **Bethesda**. El sindicato que representa a los empleados de **Bethesda** destacó que los despidos afectaron a programadores, artistas, diseñadores y testers, subrayando el costo humano detrás de estos anuncios ambiciosos. Sin embargo, el entusiasmo por **Fallout 5** y las remasterizaciones confirmadas sugiere un fuerte deseo de la comunidad de regresar a los paisajes irradiados, a pesar de los desafíos detrás de escena.

## Próximos pasos

Aunque **Fallout 5** está confirmado para estar en preproducción, no se han anunciado ventanas de lanzamiento o plataformas específicas. Los fanáticos pueden esperar más detalles a medida que **Bethesda Game Studios** continúa delineando su hoja de ruta a largo plazo, que también incluye **The Elder Scrolls VI** como un enfoque de desarrollo principal.

content_raw: Video game development never changes, it seems. Quick on the heels of Microsoft announcing that it was instituting sweeping layoffs across many of the gaming studios it owns , one of the most prominent, Bethesda Softworks, has announced that it’s launching straight into preproduction on what promises to be an absolutely massive title: Fallout 5 , the first main series entry in the post-apocalyptic action-RPG franchise since  Fallout 4  arrived back in 2015 . This is per a new report from  Bloomberg News ‘ Jason Schreier , who talked to Bethesda studio head Todd Howard about the plans to push forward with with what will inevitably be a monumental project, despite Bethesda now working with a recently gutted staff. The studio was one of several Microsoft-owned studios to be targeted in layoffs that ultimately affected some 1,600 employees in its Xbox gaming division, including its sister studio, ZeniMax Online Studios, which develops the online version of the studio’s popular Elder Scrolls  franchise. It sounds like Bethesda was hit  slightly  less hard than some other Xbox studios—Schreier’s report notes that it lost “dozens” of staff, as opposed to the hundreds laid off at other teams—but it’s still kind of wild that the studio is publicizing that it’s embarking on one of the biggest games in its history at this exact, “Please don’t look too closely at the wreckage” moment. To be fair, Fallout is having a watershed moment right now, as Prime Video’s TV adaptation has helped build interest in its post-apocalyptic satire of American life. (Even as Microsoft has had nowhere “new” to filter incoming players besides Bethesda’s very messy online game Fallout 76 . ) That renewed interest—and the fact that Fallout 5  will take many years to complete—presumably helps explain why Bethesda has also recently tapped its fellow Microsoft subsidiary Obsidian Entertainment to craft a new game in the universe, scheduled to arrive well ahead of Fallout 5 . (Obsidian—which also lost a big chunk of its staff in these layoffs, and was reportedly ordered to move off of projects focused on its own original IP —was founded by many of the people who made the first few Fallout  games, before Bethesda revived the franchise with the blockbuster  Fallout 3 ; the studio last touched the franchise with 2010’s  Fallout: New Vegas , a cult favorite that served as the plot inspiration for the most recent season of the show.)  Howard, who’s been with Bethesda since it was a plucky little independent studio making groundbreaking computer RPGs like  The Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall , called the recent layoffs “really tough.” (The crowds of protestors who’ve gathered around the company’s studios over the last week to protest the layoffs would presumably agree.)
